reviews.originalVerification: x tan(x)=1 is even and has no root at zero or the tangent poles. For x>0 in [0,2pi], the positive tangent branches (0,pi/2) and (pi,3pi/2) each cross decreasing 1/x once; negative branches cannot. Reflection gives four roots total, option E. Endpoints fail the original equation. Exact interval and official E checked.

reviews.originalVerification: Let t=tan x, so sin2x=2t/(1+t^2) and cos2x=(1-t^2)/(1+t^2). On positive x, sin2x<cos2x requires x<pi/8, where tan x<sin2x; on negative x, cos2x<tan x would require x<-pi/4, where tan x<sin2x. Thus sin2x<cos2x<tan x is impossible. The other orders occur on open intervals separated by the curve crossings. This is an ordering task, not modulus-quadratic root counting; reject its proposed follow-up edge.
reviews.candidateVerification: Zeros of the two factors are x=2pi/3 and x=pi/4,3pi/4. Ordering them gives product signs plus,minus,plus,minus on the four open parts of (0,pi). Thus the union is (pi/4,2pi/3) and (3pi/4,pi), D. All factor zeros are excluded by strict negativity.

independentEndpointDerivations.JZ-MOCK-E-P2-Q04: Squaring the nonnegative sum and applying sin²x+cos²x=1 gives |sin x cos x|=0. The distinct allowed inputs are 0, π/2, π and 3π/2; their sum is 3π, answer E. The excluded upper endpoint 2π is not counted.
independentEndpointDerivations.2022-P1-Q01: Let u=cos²x. The equation factors as (2u−3)(u−1)=0. Since 0≤u≤1, only u=1 is possible. Thus cos x=±1; on the stated closed interval 0≤x≤2π the roots are 0,π,2π, giving three roots and option C.
